body:
The tenets of the book you mention written by 
a Vonnegut character reminds of Eric Hoffer.
If TK didn't read Vonnegut, maybe both read Hoffer,
who wrote:
	
	"A movement is pioneered by men of words,
 materialized by fanatics and consolidated by men 
of action.
	It is usually an advantage to a movement, and perhaps
 a prerequisite for its endurance, that these roles 
should be played by different men succeeding each 
other as conditions require.
		Eric Hoffer, The True Believer (1963)

On an unrelated note, I don't think Kaczynski would
appreciate abstract expressionism.  He wrote

	ï¿½Art forms that appeal to modern leftist 
intellectuals tend to focus on sordidness, defeat 
and despair, or else they take an orgiastic tone,
throwing off rational control as if there were no 
hope of accomplishing anything through rational 
calculation and all that was left was to  immerse 
oneself in the sensations of the moment.ï¿½
	Industrial Society And Its Future,  (para. 17)
